name: Moose Plateau
description: Moose Plateau is a large rocky world whose surface is dominated by vast elevated tablelands separated by canyon systems of breathtaking depth. Ancient riverbeds and ocean basins score the lowlands, their dry channels filled with fine sediment that speaks of water lost to space over millions of years. The thin atmosphere retains just enough pressure to allow liquid water in the deepest canyons during the warmest hours, creating transient pools that evaporate by nightfall and refreeze before dawn.

The plateaus are flat and featureless for hundreds of kilometers, their horizons broken only by the dark lines of canyon rims and the occasional mesa rising like an island from the stone sea. The air is thin enough to see stars at midday near the poles, and the cold has a patient, penetrating quality that finds every gap in thermal protection. Microbial colonies cling to existence in the canyon-floor pools, their populations fluctuating with the daily water cycle in a rhythm of freezing, thawing, and desperate reproduction.

A terraforming initiative has placed atmospheric processors at strategic points across the equatorial plateaus, slowly thickening the atmosphere and raising the surface temperature. The project is in its early decades and the effects are subtle, but measurements show a consistent trend toward habitability. The microbial populations have responded unpredictably to the changing conditions, with some colonies thriving and others declining as the chemistry of their ephemeral pools shifts.

Moose Plateau represents a long-term investment in planetary engineering, with full habitability projected in two to three centuries. The question of whether the native microbial life can survive the transformation, or whether it should be prioritized over human habitability, has become a political flashpoint. Meanwhile, the terraforming equipment requires regular maintenance and resupply, creating a steady flow of traffic to a world that offers little immediate return. Those who work on Moose Plateau are building for descendants they will never meet.
